auth.description: Zoom server-to-server OAuth access token, sent as a bearer. Minted outside flux and supplied through the environment; it expires within the hour and nothing here can refresh it
auth.name: zoom.access_token
auth.subject: unstated

description: Zoom meeting administration: cancel a meeting, and read a user. Reading and creating a meeting are withheld — both return the host's ZAK token in `start_url` (C-430)

contract.description: Cancel a meeting. It is gone — Zoom offers no undelete, and the meeting id, its join URL and any registrations go with it. Whether Zoom emails the host or the registrants about the cancellation is left to Zoom's own default; this operation cannot ask for either. A non-2xx response is returned as data, not a failure: the vendor's error message is at `/message`, its error code at `/code` in the response body.

operations.description: Cancel a meeting. It is gone — Zoom offers no undelete, and the meeting id, its join URL and any registrations go with it. Whether Zoom emails the host or the registrants about the cancellation is left to Zoom's own default; this operation cannot ask for either

params.description: The numeric id of the meeting to cancel. A meeting UUID is not accepted: a Zoom UUID is base64 that can carry `/` and would have to be double URL-encoded, and nothing in this pipeline encodes a path
params.name: meeting_id

contract.description: Get one user — their id, email, name, timezone, licence type and personal meeting id. This is how `me` is resolved to the id a meeting is created under. A non-2xx response is returned as data, not a failure: the vendor's error message is at `/message`, its error code at `/code` in the response body.

operations.description: Get one user — their id, email, name, timezone, licence type and personal meeting id. This is how `me` is resolved to the id a meeting is created under

params.description: `me` for the token's own user, a Zoom user id, or the user's email address
params.name: user_id

created_at.description: ISO 8601, not Unix seconds. For a `pending` user Zoom's docs warn this reflects the time of the API call rather than account creation

id.description: The user's Zoom id — what `me` resolves to, and the `user_id` a meeting is created under

last_login_time.description: ISO 8601, or absent for a user who never signed in

personal_meeting_url.description: The join URL for the PMI. A participant link, not a host link — contrast `start_url` on a meeting

phone_numbers.description: Each `{code, country, label, number, verified}`, where `label` is `Mobile`, `Office`, `Home` or `Fax` and `verified` here IS a boolean. Personal data. The flat `phone_number`/`phone_country` members are deprecated and are not declared

pmi.description: The personal meeting id — a standing meeting room. Reusing it means every past participant can rejoin

status.description: `pending` means the person has never activated the account — a meeting created for them still exists, but they cannot host it

timezone.description: IANA name, e.g. `Europe/Berlin`. A meeting created without an explicit timezone uses this one

type.description: THE LICENCE, AS AN INTEGER: 1 Basic, 2 Licensed, 4 Unassigned without Meetings Basic. A Basic user's group meetings are time-capped, so this is what to check before scheduling one

use_pmi.description: Whether new meetings default to the PMI rather than a fresh id

verified.description: AN INTEGER, not a boolean: 1 verified, 0 not. The `verified` inside a `phone_numbers` entry *is* a boolean
